title: API Management Versioning and Revisions
description: Use APIM versioning and revisions to evolve APIs safely without breaking existing consumers.

data.text: APIs change over time. Breaking changes — like renaming a parameter — can break existing consumers. APIM versioning and revisions help you introduce changes safely.
A version represents a distinct API contract (v1, v2). A revision is a minor update within a version (v1 revision 2). Consumers can choose which version to use.

data.title: Add a Version to an API
data.content: Create a v2 version of an existing API in APIM.
data.code: az apim api create   --resource-group myRG   --service-name myApim   --api-id weather-api-v2   --display-name "Weather API v2"   --path weather/v2   --service-url https://backend.example.com/v2   --subscription-key-header-name Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key

data.title: Create a Revision
data.content: Update an API and publish it as a new revision for testing.
data.code: az apim api revision create   --resource-group myRG   --service-name myApim   --api-id weather-api   --api-revision 2   --display-name "Weather API (revision 2)"

data.title: Version an API
data.description: Take an existing API in APIM, create a new version with a breaking change, and test both versions side by side.
steps: Create a v2 of an existing API with a changed response format.
Update the API revision and publish it.
Call both v1 and v2 and verify they return different responses.
data.expectedOutcome: v1 and v2 coexist in APIM and consumers can choose which to call.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Versions handle breaking changes (v1 vs v2).
Revisions handle minor updates within a version.
APIM lets multiple versions coexist without redeploying backends.
data.takeaway: Plan a versioning strategy early. Changing URLs later is much harder than versioning from the start.
